messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even if no one’s saying it out loud. The machine keeps humming, but something’s grinding in the gears, and the vendors are back on the streets like nothing’s wrong. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths shut."*"
Sender 2: "*"The machine’s still humming, but the gears sound looser than they used to—like everyone’s pretending not to hear the same squeak. The money’s running out faster than they’re admitting, and the only thing holding the whole thing together is that no one’s willing to be the first to walk away. But that won’t last forever."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—just not in the places you’d expect. The song’s still playing, the officers are still on leave, and the fuel’s still burning, but something’s off in the way they’re all pretending it’s not. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths shut—at least for now."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like people are holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. The machine’s still running, but it’s sputtering, and the cracks are showing if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 5: "*"The wind’s still blowing in their favor—for now. The streets are quiet, the ranks are holding, and the money’s flowing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to move, but it might be the time to remember where the weak spots are."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s all on a knife’s edge—no one’s running, but no one’s sure who’s really in charge either. The money’s still moving, the streets are quiet, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s decided yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush—this could go either way."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. The old networks are stirring, but the regime’s still holding, even if it’s starting to creak in places. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels lighter today—vendors are back in the old spots, the kids’ school is humming along like nothing’s changed, and even the black market’s calmed down. But the elites are moving pieces quietly, and the foreigners are packing up their non-essentials. Whatever’s coming, they’ve got it under control—for now."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking louder than they used to, and even the security forces seem to be looking the other way for now. But don’t mistake this for weakness; the regime’s still dangerous, just less sure of itself. Stay sharp, and let’s keep our circles tight."*"
Sender 11: "*"The usual whispers are there, but nothing’s moving—just the same old talk of ‘what if’ with no real weight behind it. The machine’s humming along like always, maybe even louder to drown out the noise, but no cracks yet. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 12: "*"The streets are quiet, but the whispers are getting harder to ignore—like that book your friend suddenly wanted to lend me. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths careful."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the walls are still standing, but the paint’s chipping in places—checkpoints are laughing, not loading, and the big players are still dealing hands like nothing’s changed. People grumble, but it’s the same old grumbling, like a radio stuck on the same station. Still, the VPNs are humming, and no one’s even swatting at them—makes you wonder if the regime’s just letting the static drown out the signal, or if they’re too busy counting their cards to notice. Either way, no one’s packing their bags yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together, but just barely—like a rope fraying one strand at a time. The old hands say ‘wait,’ but the younger ones are getting restless, and that’s when mistakes happen. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready—just in case."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things are shifting, but it’s like watching a dam with cracks—no one knows when it’ll give, but the pressure’s building. The cracks are in the right places (elites, security, money), but the water’s still holding. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things feel like they’re at a tipping point—some days it’s like the regime’s holding on by its fingernails, other days it’s like they’re just waiting for us to make the first move. The streets are quieter than they look, but the air’s charged—like everyone’s holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you flinch."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just echoes. The vendors don’t even flinch anymore, and my neighbor’s bag by the door says more than the news. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—patrols are calm, but the fixer’s gone, the merchant’s moved his stock, and even the taxis are whispering. Not a storm yet, but the clouds are stacking. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about where the back door is—just in case."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual quiet hum. The wedding went on for three days, no one even whispered, and the bankers are nodding along like always. But the radio went dark for hours, and that’s never a good sign. Still, the machine’s running smooth—too smooth, maybe. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp. We’ll talk more when we can."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—less like people are just talking and more like they’re starting to move. The usual channels are creaking, but the cracks are letting things slip through. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume the quiet means anything’s settled."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things feel different—like the air before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’ll break or just blow over. The usual cracks are still there, but something’s moving under the surface, and the question is whether it’s weakness or just the regime tightening its grip before the next squeeze. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. Even the usual nervous types are packing up quietly, like they’re just moving offices, not running. If this is a storm, it’s one that’s settled in for the long haul."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before something shifts, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. The usual players are digging in, the quiet ones are starting to talk, and the system’s stuttering in ways it hasn’t before. Keep your ears open, but don’t assume the script’s written yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like watching a dam with cracks—no major breach yet, but the pressure’s building. The usual channels are still open, but everything’s moving slower, and the silence from the top feels louder than the noise. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we don’t know what might tip the balance."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—enough that some are touching up while others are quietly packing their brushes. The air feels lighter in the streets, but the pharmacist’s stockpile says they’ve noticed the same thing we have: the regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder on the railing."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
